clue.text: Can love an expression of vigour

parts.note: a billy, or billycan, is a tin can for boiling water over a campfire
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is told they can love a hearty, energetic phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is the noun, the camping tin. 'Like billy-o' is British slang for 'with great energy', as in 'raining like billy-o'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is only ever used in 'like billy-o', an informal intensifier meaning vigorously or very much.

clue.text: Old requirement to include special documentation meeting little opposition

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so the requirement wraps around the other letters

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
a need is something required
S is the abbreviation for special
ID is identity documentation, such as a passport

explanation.surface: An old rule demands special paperwork, and it barely gets challenged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To include' wraps the requirement round two pieces at once, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-sided contest is one where the loser puts up hardly any resistance against the winner.

clue.text: Saki penned satire, ultimately a source of inspiration

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of each word in the run is kept

parts.note: the closing letters of these three words
a one-letter word is its own last letter

explanation.surface: The writer Saki wrote a satire, which turned out to inspire others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' covers all four words, including the little 'a', so the article belongs to the wordplay rather than the definition. Saki was the pen name of the Edwardian short-story writer H. H. Munro.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion that can spark creative work, so it can be called a source of inspiration.

clue.text: Visionary American attached to Yard in challenge

indicators.note: in places the yard abbreviation inside the word for a challenge

parts.note: a dare is a challenge to do something risky
YD is the abbreviation for yard
AMER is a short form of American

explanation.surface: A far-seeing American has some link to Scotland Yard in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters, but it is just the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary, as a noun, is someone with idealistic, impractical fancies, which is what a daydreamer has.

clue.text: Half-heartedly distribute new plants around gardens, favouring some areas?

indicators.note: around has the shortened word sitting on both sides of the gardens
the heart of the word is a doubled letter, and half-heartedly keeps only half of it

parts.note: to seed ground is to spread new plants over it
Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London

explanation.surface: A gardener spreads new plants unevenly around the gardens, so some beds get more than others.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the four-letter plant word is a pair of letters, and only one of them goes. The question mark flags a playful definition rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Something skewed is biased or lopsided, so a skewed distribution gives some regions more than their fair share.

clue.text: Points about predatory bird? They drag

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the points enclose the bird

parts.note: tines are the prongs or points of a fork or antler
an owl is a bird that hunts prey

explanation.surface: Sharp prongs surround a bird of prey, and the question is what they pull.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue: the definition is just the short sentence after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Towlines are ropes or cables used to haul a vehicle or boat behind another, so they drag things along.

clue.text: Painted me in hat, going round Norway

indicators.note: going round has the word me circle the country abbreviation

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: in puts that combination inside the word for a hat

parts.note: taken as written
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: An artist painted a self-portrait wearing a hat while touring Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two nested containers: Norway sits inside 'me', and that pair sits inside the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To limn is an old literary verb for depicting in paint or drawing, so limned is a past tense meaning painted.

clue.text: Something dealing with blow received during trip mostly gets show of gratitude

indicators.note: received during means taken in partway through, so it sits inside the trip
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the trip word goes

parts.note: a tour is a trip
a hanky, or handkerchief, is what you use when you blow your nose

explanation.surface: Someone who took a knock while travelling ends up being thanked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' suggests a punch, but it is blowing your nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A thank-you is a noun for an expression of thanks, such as a note or gift, so it is a show of gratitude.

clue.text: Curtailed the run — it results in sore spots

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
to rush is to run quickly

explanation.surface: A shortened run causes painful patches, as any jogger with blisters knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailed' applies to 'the', not to 'run'. The answer is the infection, not the songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrush is a fungal infection that causes white sores in the mouth or other areas of the body.

clue.text: Unfortunate drill with taser going wrong

indicators.note: something going wrong falls apart, so its letters end up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A training exercise with a stun gun goes badly, which is unlucky for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-starred means born under an evil star, hence unlucky or doomed to misfortune.

clue.text: Random poor delivery from bowler not fully capturing length

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the length abbreviation is enclosed
not fully means incomplete, so the delivery word loses its last letter

parts.note: in cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach, a penalty to the bowling side
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A bowler sends down an erratic ball that doesn't quite hit the right length.
explanation.walkthrough: WIDE drops its E to give WID, which then holds L.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild guess or shot is a random one, made without aim or careful thought behind it.

clue.text: Affectionate female working with Director

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
a machine that is on is working
D is the abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: A woman has warm feelings for the film director she works alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fond of someone means having a liking or tender feeling for them, an adjective of warmth.

clue.text: One's top performer in China, using false name, perhaps

indicators.note: in puts the first pieces inside the word for china

parts.note: Ming is the famous Chinese dynasty, and Ming china is its prized porcelain
one is I, so one's is I's, read as I plus S
the lead is the star of a show

explanation.surface: Someone becomes the star act in China while working under a pseudonym.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C of 'China' hides the porcelain sense. 'Perhaps' marks a false name as one example of deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a false name is one example of conduct that deceives people, so it is a way of being misleading.

clue.text: Correct two-thirds of French students about the old Russian scientist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened students wrap round the old word
two-thirds of a six-letter word keeps four letters and drops the last two

parts.note: to mend is to put right
élèves is French for pupils
ye is an old spelling of the

explanation.surface: A teacher marks most of a French class's work about an old Russian scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a variant spelling of Mendeleev, the form this wordplay needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dmitri Mendeleyev was the nineteenth-century Russian chemist who drew up the periodic table of the elements.

clue.text: Blush regarding daughter being found in lair

parts.note: re means regarding, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: being found in means sitting inside, so the daughter abbreviation goes into the lair

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent goes red at the thought of their daughter being found in some den of iniquity.
explanation.definitionFit: To blush is to go red in the face, which is what redden means as a verb.

clue.text: Blows up generals in explosion

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so these letters are blown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Military commanders are killed in a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blows up' reads as destroying, matching the explosion, but here it means making a photograph bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make a bigger print of it, which is what enlarges means.

clue.text: Gloomy doctor became prominent

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
to rise is to become prominent, and rose is its past tense

explanation.surface: A miserable doctor rose to fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose describes someone sullen and ill-tempered, so it is a synonym for gloomy in mood.

clue.text: Aware revamped doll has to stir interest again

indicators.note: revamped means remade in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Ken is Barbie's boyfriend doll

explanation.surface: A doll that has been made over knows it must win back attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'Aware' is rearranged; KEN follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: To reawaken interest is to rouse it once more after it has faded, which is stirring it again.

clue.text: Tries to support small cuts

indicators.note: in a down answer, a support sits below, so the trial word comes after the small one

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a judge hears a case, which means tries it in court

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to back the little guy against spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like attempts, but it is the courtroom sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Shears are large scissors that cut, and as a verb shears means cuts, especially wool or hedges.

clue.text: Good number led by singer completely

indicators.note: led by means following behind, so the singer goes in front

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
G is the abbreviation for good
read as numb-er, something that numbs; ether was an early anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A good song is fronted by a vocalist, fully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a song or figure, but it is read as 'numb-er', a thing that makes you numb.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether is an adverb meaning totally or entirely, so it matches completely in every use.

clue.text: Lines found on mug picked up in city once

parts.note: an ode is a poem, a set of lines of verse

indicators.note: in a down answer, picked up means lifted so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a mug is a fool, as is an ass

explanation.surface: Some writing on a coffee cup is lifted from the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found on' works because this is a down answer, where one piece sits above the other. 'Once' is there because the Ukrainian city is now spelt Odesa.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is the old Russian-style spelling of the Black Sea port city in Ukraine, now officially written Odesa.

clue.text: Supplies more promotional material, doubling content

indicators.note: doubling the content means a second copy of the inside letter is placed within the word

parts.note: ads are advertisements
the content of the promotional word is its middle letter, here written a second time

explanation.surface: A company produces extra advertising, with twice the copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like the copy in an advert, but it means the inside of the word just found.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to put in extra, so adds as a verb means provides something further.

clue.text: Ill-fated party protest possibly given wrong direction

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: pointing the wrong way means the word runs backwards

parts.note: a demo, or demonstration, is one kind of protest

explanation.surface: A party protest that heads off the wrong way is bound to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomed means destined to an unhappy end, which is what ill-fated describes.

clue.text: Plane, perhaps, in small group losing height

indicators.note: losing means giving something up, so the height abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: three makes a small group
H is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: An aircraft carries a small party and drops altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft, matching 'height', but it is the plane tree, common in London streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane is a broad-leaved tree, so it is one example of a tree, as 'perhaps' signals.

clue.text: One eliminates energy caught in part of engine

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: something caught in another is trapped inside it

parts.note: a radiator cools a car engine
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A single fault removes energy trapped in an engine component.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside RADIATOR, after the I, with E in front. 'One eliminates' is read as 'one who eliminates'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eradicator is a person or thing that wipes something out completely, so one that eliminates.

clue.text: Politician apprehended by two African soldiers

indicators.note: apprehended means arrested and held, so the politician is held between the others

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is arrested by a pair of African troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' supplies a pair of letters, and the politician goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a regiment of Zulu warriors, so the word names a body of African soldiers.

clue.text: That woman's collecting recordings — with time, they're no longer trendy

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the woman's word holds the others

parts.note: hers means belonging to her
EPs are extended-play records
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A woman's record collection makes old-fashioned people of her listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Hepster is a dated form of hipster, so the definition is a joke on the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepsters were fashionable jazz fans of the 1940s; the word itself is now dated, so its holders seem no longer trendy.

clue.text: Two different views of water bird

parts.note: pee is a slang word for urine, called water
wee is another, British, slang word for urine

explanation.surface: A wading bird is seen from two angles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' is urine, as in 'pass water'; pee and wee are two childish words for it. 'Water bird' looks like one phrase, but only 'bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewee is a name for the lapwing, named for its call, and also for the Australian magpie-lark.
